It covers the fundamental concepts and dimensions of privacy, the regulatory requirements, and various management tools to comply with data protection laws and meet public expectation. Through the analysis of privacy impacts on a number of new technologies such as artificial intelligence, blockchain, cloud, data analytics and their applications, students may learn how to respect individuals’ privacy when applying technologies.
cl: Explain the fundamental tension in data and privacy protection and development.
Discuss privacy in the dimensions of secrecy, seclusion and autonomy/freedom.
Discuss data protection law as a protector of individual rights and facilitator for commerce.
Compare and contrast different data protection regimes and regulations.
Recognize the limitation of the law, impacts of technological changes and the expectation of the public.
Explain how to apply relevant management tools to demonstrate commitments on privacy and data protection.
Identify the privacy challenges and benefits of technological developments and manage them at the work context.
Identify the common challenges, mistakes, and management lessons in data protection and privacy management from real-life cases, and apply/articulate them in future cases.

ISOM5240.d: Deep Learning (DL) is a promising way for developing Artificial Intelligence (AI) applications. It is exceptionally useful for training a large amount of unstructured historical datasets, and predicting the most-likely outputs. DL can be applied in many business areas such as finance, marketing, customer services, information security and so on, and most importantly DL can outperform existing non-AI systems due to the nature of neural networks. This course intends to introduce Python programming language for developing DL business applications. Students will apply knowledge in current and future trends of DL to design DL business applications.
cl: Apply Python programming to develop deep learning business applications.
Describe and differentiate deep learning models.
Explain the logic of deep learning business applications written in Python.

ISOM5250.d: This course introduces students to business application modeling using Visual Basic Applications (VBA) in Excel. Students will learn to develop applications in different business areas, including finance, marketing, technology operations, etc. Essential features of VBA needed for application development will be introduced as part of the course and hence no prior experience with VBA is needed. Emphasis is on extensive hands-on problem solving.
cl: Explain object oriented programming (OOP) concepts.
Model business problems logically.
Develop programming solutions to business problems.
Write computer programs with common programming practices.
Identify and fix logical and runtime errors in computer programs.

ISOM5260.d: Introduction to database management systems with emphasis on business applications. Technical and administrative considerations in database implementation. Students implement a business system using a commercial-off-the-shelf software package.
cl: Define the basic concepts of database environment and describe the development process.
Analyze and design a database using Entity Relationship Diagram (ERD) and Enhanced Entity Relationship Diagram.
Analyze how data can be represented and stored in a typical business information system through normalization concept.
Insert, manipulate, and analyze the data in a database using structured query language (SQL) and Oracle database.
Organize and evaluate different database administration concepts and procedures.

ISOM5270.d: Data plays an increasingly important role in business decision making. This course introduces the key concepts and applications of business analytics in the world of Big Data. Example business problems to be solved analytically include customer relationship management, financial trading, social media marketing, search engine strategy, etc. Hands-on experience with popular data analytical tools will be included.
cl: Approach business problems data-analytically (intelligently). Think carefully & systematically about whether & how data can improve business performance.

Interact competently on the topic of data analytics. Know the basics of data mining processes, techniques, & systems well enough to interact with business analysts, marketers, and clients. Be able to envision Big Data opportunities.
Identify the right Big Data techniques for various business problems. Gain hands-on experience in using popular data analysis tools.

ISOM5280.d: In-depth study of information systems security in business organizations. Basic principles and functions of secure systems reviewed; management policy, plans and programs discussed.
cl: Identify information security trends and developments.
Classify common security threats and describe the characteristics of each type of threats.
Apply protection tools to enhance organizational information security.
Design proper information security solutions to minimize different security risks.
Identify common mistakes in information security management.
Describe the key features of cyber-crimes and how they threaten information assets and the security of organizations.
Characterize different approaches to tackling cyber-crimes and their key principles.
Describe the key purpose and processes of computer forensics.
Analyze the options available to an organization when it is under security threats.

ISOM5290.d: This course provides an overview of the main aspects of information systems (IS) development with a focus on defining/modeling the business requirements following the Unified Modeling Language (UML) standard. Major topics include use case modeling, object-oriented modeling, data flow and process diagramming, and the key management issues and methodologies in IS development.
cl: Analyze the core issues and identify factors that are critical to the development of Information systems.
Compare and contrast IS development methodologies.
Define and explain system analysis and modeling.
Diagnose key IS development management issues and make sound IS development decisions as business managers.

ISOM5310.d: The use of artificial intelligence (AI) becomes an emerging trend in various business areas and industries, as its power to transform operations, customer experiences, and management is exponential. Harnessing AI’s potential for competitive performance requires a new type of professionals, who understand how machine learning (ML) works, what they can deliver and how they can be applied into different business context. This course is intended to bridge the gap between the business strategy and technical how-to. Through lectures, case discussion, and experiments in real-world data sets, students will gain a broad understanding of ML and AI concepts, explore the state-of-art use cases of AI technology in business, identify new opportunities and potential risks brought by AI, and recognize how to effectively communicate with the data science and machine learning team.
cl: Explain the core technical attributes of machine learning and artificial intelligence (AI).
Identify current AI development trends.
Connect business insights to technological possibilities of AI.
Navigate the ethical and societal implications of AI projects.
Facilitate effective communication between technical and managerial teams.

ISOM5320.d: This course offers essential knowledge and tools for managers of digital business. Topics include e-commerce models, web analytics, Internet marketing, Internet pricing and strategy, web-based personalization, online-intermediaries, etc.
cl: Describe how a business organization’s choices of strategy and process are closely related to its information management and communications capabilities in the context of digital business.
Develop quantitative and analytical techniques to solve business problems with innovative perspectives.
Analyze the core technological and business issues and identify critical factors for business decision-making with the context of digital business.
Evaluate information systems relations with strategy, process, organization and market.

ISOM5330.d: This course provides students with an overview of the underlying information technologies used in the finance, banking, and insurance industries. The course covers the critical business, legal and technology issues and the related risks faced by corporate executives when analyzing, designing, launching and managing Financial Technology projects to drive business innovations.
cl: Explain what FinTech is and the underlying ICT (Information Communication Technology) that supports the disruptive business strategies/models.
Explore and assess the threats and the business opportunities in the innovative finance landscape with Artificial Intelligence, big data, blockchain and distributed ledger technology (DLT).

Critically examine the innovative FinTech business models, ICT and their respective critical success factors, risks, compliance and legislative frameworks related to Crowd Funding, Fast Payment, Financial Intelligence, Quantitative Finance, Algorithmic Trading and High Frequency Trading for institutional/professional traders vs. retail traders, and Robo-Traders.
Lead FinTech development teams when dealing with stakeholders from business, IT, legal, audit and the regulators.
Manage global FinTech and InsurTech projects and be part of the senior executive team.

ISOM5340.d: Recent technology innovations have reshaped the finance industry, leading to new way of how financial information is disseminated, processed and analyzed. Topics to be covered will include: artificial intelligence in financial analytics, big data alpha models, algorithm trading and high frequency trading, social trading, robo-advisor, P2P lending, cryptocurrency and blockchain.
cl: Describe the emerging trend of technology-enabled financial applications.
Explain the quantitative trading with big data.
Explain the role of artificial intelligence in financial applications.
Define the mechanism behind the Cryptocurrency.
Conduct basic financial analytics with Python programming language.

ISOM5360.d: This course introduces the fundamental concepts of information systems (IS) auditing.  Topics include IS control and assurance, COBIT, business continuity planning, protection of information assets, auditing the network infrastructure, physical access exposures and controls, and disaster recovery management.
cl: Develop and implement a risk-based IT audit strategy in compliance with IT audit standards to ensure that key areas are included.
Plan specific audits to determine whether information systems are protected, controlled and provide value to the organization.
Conduct audits in accordance with IT audit standards to achieve planned audit objectives.
Evaluate the effectiveness of the IT governance structure to determine whether IT decisions, directions and performance support the organization's strategies and objectives.

Evaluate the organization's IT policies, standards, and procedures, and the processes for their development, approval, implementation, maintenance, and monitoring, to determine whether they support the IT strategy and comply with regulatory and legal requirements.
Evaluate the organization's business continuity plan to determine the organization's ability to continue essential business operations during the period of an IT disruption.
Evaluate the business case for proposed investments in information systems acquisition, development, maintenance and subsequent retirement to determine whether it meets business objectives.
Evaluate the project management practices and controls to determine whether business requirements are achieved in a cost-effective manner while managing risks to the organization.
Evaluate the information security policies, standards and procedures for completeness and alignment with generally accepted practices.
Evaluate the design, implementation and monitoring of physical access and environmental controls to determine whether information assets are adequately safeguarded.

ISOM5370.d: Technology and innovation management (TIM) plays an important role in enhancing the competitiveness of firms, industries, and even nations.  This course provides a comprehensive introduction to TIM from strategic perspectives and addresses key issues such as technology and innovation decision making, open innovation system, lead user innovation, intellectual property portfolio management, and national innovation system.  Specifically, it will highlight how technology can facilitate corporate innovation.  Students will obtain basic skills in formulating TIM-based competitive strategies.
cl: Stimulate their curiosity and broaden their perspective by critically analyzing puzzling critical dilemmas that deny some long-held assumptions.
Recognize various concepts and frameworks to explain different aspects of technological innovation from the business strategy perspective.
Apply the concepts and theoretical frameworks learned from the course to analyze the innovation of a chosen company and propose sound and implementable recommendations to the company.

ISOM5390.d: This course examines how firms can use digital marketing and social media to reach, acquire, and engage customers. Topics include search and display ads, viral marketing analytics, online word-of-mouth, social data, and mobile ads and apps, etc.
cl: Explain key concepts in digital and social media strategy.
Develop strategies for viral campaigns.
Implement strategies for handling negative online word-of-mouth.
Develop strategies to engage customers in a mobile-driven economy.
Conduct analyses to support digital/social media strategies and activities.

ISOM5400.d: Introductory core course for MPhil and PhD students majoring or minoring in information systems; overview of the conduct of research in the information systems field. Advanced master degree students may register with the approval of the instructor.
cl: Formulate problems to develop research questions.
Achieve correspondence between conceptual and empirical specifications of variance models.
Apply maching learning of structured and unstructured data in the design of variance studies.
Understand construct/scale development and validation.
Do survey design and administration.
Review and discuss examples of experiments in the MIS literature.
Design an experiment in a content area of interest.
Understand what social networks are and history of social network theory and analysis.
Discuss what can be studied from a social network perspective.

ISOM5410.d: This course focuses on ethics and governance in the field of artificial intelligence (AI) and Generative AI within the financial services sector. It examines how the GenAI systems and the way they are being trained pose a number of challenges regarding ethical use of data and systems as well as the impact their results might have, both as problem solver in risk management and data processing, and also as attack vector in the hands of fraudsters. Students will learn how to implement reliable, well-governed GenAI pipelines in corporate environments.
cl: Understand the construction principles of GenAI systems and how they give rise to a number of challenges and issues.
Know the privacy and ethical concerns when using data for training and inference.
Be familiar with regulatory requirements for AI and GenAI deployments.
Know how a stringent governance process in a company ensures regulatory compliance and minimization of risk.
Know how to assess GenAI results and be aware of ways to use GenAI in both beneficial and also fraudulent ways.

ISOM5420.d: Students compete in operating and managing a virtual business as teams using the CapStone Business Simulation software that has been adopted by more than 500 business schools and universities worldwide.  This team-based competition using business simulation tools provide an active-learning, hands-on business management experience integrating strategy, finance, marketing, accounting, human resources training and operations management perspectives for operating a complete business enterprise.
cl: Identify the differences between strategy formulation and execution.
Explain the relations between different tactical decisions.
Explain how each functional/tactical decision affects the success of an organization.
Appreciate the challenges faced by large organizations and the connection between strategy and organizational portfolio of assets and products.
Compare and contrast different analytical tools and their applications.
Compare and contrast the options available to a business in view of the global trends.
Formulate, analyze, and execute a strategy for a virtual company.
Explain how the performance of a company should be assessed and tied to the design and execution of competitive strategies.

ISOM5430.d: The use of artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) becomes an emerging trend in various business functions and industries for their exponential power to generate revenues, automate operations, improve customer experiences, and transform business management. Through lectures, case discussion and experiments in real-world data sets, students will gain a broad understanding of ML and AI concepts, explore the state-of-art cloud-native system design patterns, and recognize good practice in machine learning system development and deployment.
cl: Understand the core technical attributes of ML and AI.
Recognize the current trends in automated ML.
Identify the key components of the ML production lifecycle and pipeline.
Adopt best practices in ML production and continuous system operation.

ISOM5440.d: Recent breakthroughs in Large Language Models (LLMs) have made deep-learning-based Natural Language Processing a business imperative, reshaping workflows and decision-making across industries. This course aims to provide a comprehensive introduction to cutting-edge neural approaches for NLP. Students will learn how to design, train, and fine-tune models using Python for various business applications such as sentiment analysis, summarization, and conversational AI.
cl: Apply deep learning methods to tackle real-world Natural Language Processing (NLP) problems.
Demonstrate familiarity with key concepts and theoretical frameworks in Deep Learning and NLP, and understand their interplay in driving the recent AI boom.
Design and implement programming solutions for practical NLP challenges in the business domain.
Fine-tune pre-trained Large Language Models (e.g., BERT, GPTs, T5) and adapt them for customized business applications.

ISOM5450.d: This course is designed for students from different professions to become skilled in using consulting tools to analyze issues, evaluate solutions from multiple dimensions of people, process, technology and governance, and then use a framework for IT strategy recommendations for effective communication.  Students will learn how to apply these technology consulting tools to the latest technology trends, such as big data, e-commerce, e-recruitment, security, etc. facing today's businesses.
cl: Think critically and structure arguments logically.
Internalize consulting methodologies with hands-on practice.
Analyze the mindset of consultants and decision-makers.
Improve communication, public speaking and rejection handling.

ISOM5460.d: This course covers the essential project management skills to ensure successful implementation of high-technology projects.  Topics include investment decisions, resource planning, budgeting, scheduling, outsourcing, and risk assessment and control, as major components of the PMBOK (Project Management Body of Knowledge).
cl: Analyze the core issues in project management and identify critical success factors.
Solve several project management problems with appropriate tools and techniques.
Compare and contrast different project management methodologies.
Identify the major project deliverables and when they are due.

ISOM5470.d: This course focuses on developing tech businesses in Asia and China, home to two-thirds of the world’s population and rapidly growing markets, through a series of focused case studies and sharing from guest speakers with firsthand experience in such development.
cl: Articulate the technology business opportunities and challenges across Asia and China.
Describe how government policies support and accelerate (or limit) technology business development across Asia and China.
Discuss and compare technology businesses in several sectors across Asia and China.
Apply business strategy and planning tools in assessing technology businesses in Asia and China.
Identify, articulate, and discuss critical success factors in developing technology businesses.

ISOM5480.d: This course introduces the principles of technology entrepreneurship.  It provides an overview of the theory and best practices on developing innovative business models of the digital economy, and the strategy, structure and pricing related to new enterprises.  Topics include technology entrepreneurship, e-marketing, web 2.0 and enterprise 2.0, information in financial market, globalization, and the long tail.
cl: Analyze the core issues and identify critical factors for business decision-making in an entrepreneurship setting.
Approach business problems from alternative and innovative perspectives.
Develop management skills in the context of information systems and solve startup management issues.
Facilitate business innovations via the use of information systems.
Interpret current technology trends and develop plans to leverage these trends.
Communicate with different audiences, including managers, end-users, investors, and other stakeholders using both technical language and business language.

ISOM5490.d: In this course, students will learn the necessary technical backgrounds and business insights to become leaders in the AI-transformed economy. We will rely on studies of technological innovation and digitization, as well as real business examples, to build a coherent framework to conceptualize the impact of AI in various settings.
cl: Learn the necessary technical backgrounds and business insights to become leaders in the AI-transformed economy.
Develop a deep understanding of the potential of AI to transform the business landscape and the tools to navigate this rapidly changing field confidently.
Apply the knowledge and tools to tackle the complex challenges of the AI-transformed economy.

ISOM5510.d: Covers various discrete and continuous probability models and their applications in business problems, estimation and testing of hypotheses, simple and multiple linear regression analysis.
cl: Recognize and describe statistical methods typically used in the analysis of business data.

ISOM5535.d: This course presents classical and modern approaches for analyzing multivariate and high dimensional data, including principal components, factor analysis, discriminant analysis, clustering, new developments on dimension reduction, large-scale covariance matrix estimation and multiple testing. All of these approaches will be covered in the context of Marketing, Finance and other important business decisions. Computational issues for both traditional and new methodologies will also be discussed.
cl: Use the concepts underlying the quantitative tools which deal with multivariate and high dimensional data, and put those tools together with data to draw meaningful conclusions.
Employ classic and advanced approaches used in multivariate and high dimensional data to different areas of business, including terminology and issues specific to finance, marketing, and economics.

ISOM5540.d: Axioms of probability, conditional probability and independence, permutations and combinations, density and distribution functions, examples of random variables, independence of random variables, transformations of random variables, order statistics, expected value, variance, higher moments; Chebychev's inequality, convergence concepts, moment generating functions, central limit theorem.  Graded P or F.
cl: Understand the role of probability in business modelling.
Improve problem solving skills and ability to think critically and independently.
Develop the capability of using probability for understanding complex data structures in business related fields.

ISOM5550.d: Properties of a random sample, sufficient statistics. Point and interval estimation, hypothesis testing, optimality of estimators and tests, linear regression and analysis of variance.
cl: Learn foundations of common statistical approaches for analyzing business data.
Improve problem solving skills and ability to think critically and independently.
Identify various techniques suitable for analyzing conplex data structures in business related fields.
Develop knowledge to understand further specialized analytical techniques for specific areas of business studies.

ISOM5580.d: In this course, we will investigate the technology and business of AI in theory and practice. We will examine what really AI is, how businesses should use it - and how they shouldn't. The reality is that AI isn't as complicated as everyone seems to be making it and that all Business Analytics graduates should be able to explain it to their colleagues, bosses, and customers. Students will have this ability by the end of the course, in addition to the capability of building simple but powerful AI tools, platforms, and agents.
cl: Explain the fundamental concepts of AI, its capabilities and limitations, and its potential impact on business.
Explain how AI differs from human cognition, and how AI may complement and/or disrupt such cognition.
Analyze the proper role of AI in teams and organizations using network theory, complexity theory, data and AI governance, and other relevant frameworks.
Communicate effectively about AI, its role in society, and its broader social, economic, and ethical implications.
Build and implement simple and even advanced AI applications for business-related data science purposes.

ISOM5600.d: The course consists of twofold: 1) Refreshment of basic accounting and finance, statistics, and programming skills for students to apply to the MSc in Business Analytics program; and 2) Develop and broaden students' creative mindset, business sense, and communication through training in data management, design thinking, and business communication. In-class exercises and assignments may be required depending on individual workshop design. An exemption for partial workshop training may be granted if students fulfill the exemption requirement. Graded PP, P or F.
cl: Understand the fundamental building blocks of statistics.
Apply basic accounting, and finance knowledge for data analysis.
Understand and apply the core foundational concept of data management.
Communicate and present business solutions with data.
Enhance creative mindset through a good understanding of design thinking.
Apply storytelling and pitching skills in business ideas presentation.

ISOM5610.d: This course describes multiple regression method and its variants as exploratory and predictive models for fact-based management and data-driven decision making. The course adopts case-based approach.
cl: Use business analytics to formulate and solve business problems and to support managerial decision making.
Identify the processes needed to develop, report, and analyze business data.
Apply selected business analytics software.

ISOM5620.d: This course focuses on various visualization analysis tools for business decisions. Making good use of visual analytics helps summarize and analyze large amount of data effectively. In this course, the topics like visualization framework, visual analytics for spatial, temporal, network and textual data, and dynamic visualization will be included. Reporting visualization results for business decisions will also be discussed.
cl: Create a visualization framework and workflow for companies.
Make use of open-source and common visualization analytics tools.
Analyze various types of data using visualization analytics for interactive knowledge exchange and for building business strategies.
Generate visualization reports for business decision making.

ISOM5630.d: The course intends to introduce students to modern data analysis using R, with an emphasis on business, in particular, financial applications. Main topics to be covered include data exploration methods, regression analysis and time series analysis.
cl: Apply modern data analysis tools ( data exploration methods, modern regression and time sense) to analyze business data.
Analyze business data, in particular financial data, and use statistical software R to do estimation, modeling, and forecasting.

ISOM5640.d: The course presents concepts of social media and networks, methods and techniques to explore and analyze the data crawled from social media and network, and business application of data mining of social network. All these will be discussed in the context of finance and marketing. Python is the unique programming language for all cases and projects.
cl: Smoothly use python to crawl social media data, and to visualize network data.
Take network modeling into account when exploring finance and marketing problems.
Identify topics and trend in the social media.

ISOM5650.d: This course is about how to preprocess real business data using Python (mainly using pandas), identify and predict the patterns of data and finally explore the real-world application of these patterns.
cl: Analyze the real business case by utilizing the Python knowledge.
Identify and extract missing values, import and export data, merge or concatenate data.
Develop new variables from the data with all kinds of pandas methods.
Evaluate the performance of models with practical standards.
Apply basic modeling in different business scenarios.

ISOM5690.d: The BA enrichment workshops aim to develop students’ business mindset and understand the landscape of analytics works across different industries. Students are expected to attend the workshops regularly in accordance with the course requirements. No assignment or exam will be required. Graded P or F.
cl: Recognize the role of data analytics processes in different industries.
Identify the current market trend and development of different sectors.
Identify the critical issues and challenges of analytical functions in business.
Discuss and analyze real business cases.
Enhance communication skills in a real business environment.

ISOM5700.d: Introduction to management of business processes that produce goods or services: topics include operations strategy, process analysis, queuing systems, inventory management, quality management, process improvement and other important issues.
cl: Explain operations from a general management perspective and the link between operations and business models.
Apply basic concepts, performance measures, analytical tools and general principles for analyzing and managing operations.
Better manage the interface between operations and other business functions.
Systematically improve and innovate business models.
Improve problem solving and analytical skills.

ISOM5701.d: This course focuses on the critical issues in the design, production and delivery of tangible goods as well as intangible goods in the business world. Topics include process analysis, capacity and bottleneck issues, waiting time management, inventory management, quality management, lean systems, supply chain management and e-commerce. Quantitative and qualitative tools will be taught to analyze the problems and create innovative solutions.
cl: Apply the business process flow concept to represent and analyze the economic activities of service or manufacturing organizations.

Analyze and evaluate the performance of the different business processes in an organization and the systems in the organization as a whole using relevant performance measures by using some basic tools in operations management.
Critically compare and differentiate business processes in similar or different system designs to identify key business processes for continuous improvement of the system.
Design appropriate performance measures for the business processes in different organizations and the supply chains.
Integrate and evaluate the different functional activities in an organization or in a supply chain to create competitive advantages in the global market.

ISOM5715.d: This course helps students develop better analytical skills in approaching strategic and tactical business decisions. Students will learn to derive solutions or conclusions that require critical thinking, quantitative analysis, and strategic reasoning skills. These skills are essential and indispensable for major business decisions.
cl: Develop more confidence and appreciation of the quantitative reasoning skill to approach business problems, evaluate solutions, and make decisions.
Apply advanced quantitative and optimization tools to gain insights from decisions that will help improve business performance.
Make informed decisions involving risks and uncertainty using analytical techniques.
Develop the abilities of leadership and teamwork with effective communication skills in the real business world.

ISOM5720.d: Concepts and practices of enterprise resource management; enterprise resource planning systems and applications, integrated systems approach to managing major business processes, business information reports and analyses.
cl: Compare the strategic values and limitations of enterprise systems.
Discuss the basic concepts and practices of process-oriented management in a global, competitive environment.
Define the skills and knowledge to successfully implement an enterprise system in organizations.
Identify the new development of ERP software and applications for facilitating e-business.
Demonstrate examples of business process integration through the use of ERP core applications and modules.
Identify the tangible benefits of enterprise integration for decision making using ERP in a simulated environment.

ISOM5725.d: This course focuses on concepts and tools that can generate operational excellence for the production and delivery of services across various industries including health care, ride-hailing, advertising, and content markets. Unlike traditional product markets, a salient feature of these industries is that services are intangible and not storable, and often highly variable, which raises significant challenges in decision making. The goal of this course is to improve the understanding of these challenges and to learn how to overcome the obstacles with data-driven quantitative models. This class will introduce simple predictive and prescriptive methods that are useful in service operations.
cl: Identify issues in service operations through descriptive analytics.
Predict future business outcomes using statistical models.
Address real-world challenges with optimization and simulation techniques.
Effectively present problems and data-driven solutions to businesses.

ISOM5730.d: Supply chain uncertainty and market fluctuation, information distortion and visibility, supply chain coordination and integration, supply chain incentives, flexibility, and design for supply chain management, supply chain strategies.
cl: Explain, evaluate and design supply chain flexibility through demand forecasting, information transparency and response time.
Explain, identify and manage the risks in supply chain sourcing and procurement.
Explain, examine and critique some critical global supply chain issues through learning and interaction with senior executives from global corporations.
Explain, examine and evaluate the sustainability, social responsibility as well as the management and decision framework of global supply chain corporations.
Explain and evaluate the impact of the evolving trends in ecommerce, O2O and other technology disruptions in supply chain management.

ISOM5740.d: This course focuses on the products and processes in the financial industries. It analyzes and evaluates the designs and performances of the internal operations and the different distribution channels of the financial institutions, and identifies opportunities for  continuous improvement in productivity and efficiency. It also covers the issues of quality control and operational risk management, the application of IT in the industry. It will also discuss the automation/outsourcing of the financial operations for non-financial institutions to improve the financial performance and risk management in the supply chain.
cl: Explain and evaluate financial markets and fund flow and distribution channels, the business processes in an economy and in the financial institutions (FI), with focus on banking industry.
Design and critique business processes for improving the productivity and service quality of the FIs.
Integrate and evaluate the different business processes and service experience in the financial organizations to create competitive advantages for the FIs.
The new development and innovations in the financial industries (fintech).
Introducing compliance, risk management for FIs and corporations.

ISOM5745.d: The course introduces the business and operations transformation approach by discussing the challenges and learning from real-life business cases. It helps students bridge the gaps between academic knowledge and real-life transformation experiences. Sharing and discussing the differences and similarities of transformation across different industry sectors will be covered.
cl: Outline a transformation program.
Conduct effective problem-solving even in industries they are not familiar with.
Have the communication and influencing toolkits that are effective in the business context.

ISOM5755.d: In today's competitive business landscape, delivering exceptional customer experience (CX) is paramount for retaining customers and maintaining profitability. This comprehensive course offers an understanding and deployment of the customer-centric strategy and customer journey mapping (CJM). The course equips students with the skills to enhance customer experience and design the end-to-end CJM's future state that differentiates them from the competition. From pre- to post-purchase interactions, this course explores the moments of truth and teaches students to create seamless, personalized, and memorable customer experiences at every step of the CJM. The course equips students with strategies and methodologies to improve customer satisfaction, loyalty, and advocacy. The course will also explore leveraging technologies like Data Science and Machine Learning through Artificial Intelligence (AI) to effectively and efficiently retain loyalty and gain new customers. Through theoretical frameworks, case studies, and workshops, students will develop the skills to analyze customer needs and pain points, design effective CJM, and implement customer-centric strategies and transformations in business-to-consumer (B2C) and business-to-business (B2B) settings.
cl: Lead and transform an organization to improve the customer-centric culture.
Create a personalized customer experience based on customer personas.
Lead and conduct a Customer Journey Mapping (CJM) exercise independently with a current company based on customer feedback and sentiments from customer feedback measurement systems.

Identify customer pain points, delighting points, moments of truth, and front and backstage stakeholders to design corrective, preventive, and predictive actions using techniques like the Jobs-To-Be-Done Laddering and 5 Whys.
Master techniques to create compelling and “wow” customer experiences throughout the CJM based on Best-In-Class industry benchmarks and research studies.
Leverage technologies like Data Analytics and Artificial Intelligent Machine Learning to enhance customer experience
Unlock the full potential of organizations’ customer-centricity and gain a competitive edge in today's experience-driven marketplace.
Design key internal leading indicators to eventual customer satisfaction.

ISOM5765.d: This course explores the practical applications of sustainability principles in the context of business operations, strategy, and innovation. Students will examine how organizations can integrate sustainability practices to create long-term value, mitigate risks, enhance competitive advantage, and contribute to addressing the grand challenge of the climate crisis. The course will cover key sustainability frameworks, tools, and best practices that can be applied across various business functions and operations.
cl: Understand core principles and significance of sustainability in business and investments.
Evaluate governance structures for transparency, accountability, and ethics.
Analyze how sustainability considerations impact product design, marketing, and operations decisions.
Evaluate the benefits and challenges of implementing sustainable practices.
Collaborate to develop sustainability action plans that align with ethical values and the interests of stakeholders.
Learn how to cultivate a culture of sustainability within an organization.
Understand the adoption of sustainability initiatives and their relevance in gaining a competitive advantage.
Spearhead the transformation of an organization into one of the most sustainable companies.

ISOM5770.d: This course covers basic concepts, tools and practices of project management. Special emphases are on project planning, scheduling, and control while addressing both the technical and the social and behavioral aspects of managing business projects.
cl: Distinguish between projects and repetitive operations.
Understand the key issues project managers face in each of the four phases in the project life cycle.
Apply tools and solutions to these issues.

ISOM5790.d: This course requires students to attend at least five industry workshops. It aims to increase students’ exposure to the operations management practices in different industries and enhance their communication skills. No assignment and exam will be needed. Graded P or F.
cl: Recognize operations/ management process in different companies/ industries.
Identify the current development and constraints of specific industries.
Discuss and analyze real business cases.
Enhance communication skills in real business environment.

ISOM5800.d: This course is open to all MBA students who need to utilize spreadsheets to create and analyze business models for decision making and/or managerial insights.  Practical exercises and case studies are used to illustrate the concepts and practices of business modeling and to build competency in using spreadsheets for advanced applications.  Graded P or F.
cl: Set up and use Excel models to derive quantitative and qualitative insights about a large spectrum of managerial problems.
Have skills around the following aspects: working with Excel; using formulas; manipulating information; analyzing business problems; identifying optimal decisions.
Have a general idea for the kinds of problems that can be tackled quantitatively, the methods available for doing so, and the relevant data that needs to be gathered.

ISOM5810.d: The science and technology of informed decision making with focus on optimizing business processes. Spreadsheet decision modeling in Excel used throughout. Emphasis on problem formulation, spreadsheet-based solution methods, and managerial insights. Applications to managerial decision problems in diverse industries and functional areas including finance and accounting, human resource, marketing, and operations.
cl: Adopt a series of quantitative models for managerial decision making.
Develop and upgrade intuition in decision making.
Develop skills of using spreadsheet in solving various management problems.

ISOM5820.d: Students shall study 12 applications in OM that  have been judged by peers as being amongst the best in recent years. They will try to understand what the problem was, how it was addressed, how it worked out and attempt to learn what marked it as a success and how portable the practice can be. The principal purpose is to expose students to a wide range of good case histories in order to enhance their repertoire and experience in OM.
cl: Contrast and analyze some of the most important problems in OM in different industries.
Contrast and critique solutions that have been used in practices.
Identify and analyze similar problems in practice; Construct solutions and defend them.
Work effectively in a team and lead a team.
Work with other functions in making operations decisions.
Communicate effectively in oral and written English in assigned task contexts.

ISOM5830.d: The course covers basic principles and approaches of computer simulation, and introduce Monte Carlo simulations with Excel and @risk, and discrete event simulation with Arena, focusing on their applications in solving business and operation problems.
cl: Develop complex simulation models.
